text: Our grandparents could tell real camphor from fake by its smell, knew that haldi and chuna make roli, and kept gond katira for the summer. They burned guggul and dhuna in the evening to clean the air of the house. Much of that knowledge has slipped out of the Indian household. In another ten years, the founder warns, people may not be able to recognise an original item at all.

text: Purifying the air the way Indian homes once did, and checking it honestly

text: In earlier times, homes were cleaned of germs with herbs and smoke rather than chemicals. Gums and resins such as guggul, dhuna and dhuwan (the resin of the Sal tree) were burned on cow-dung fire, and Bhimseni camphor was diffused through the rooms. The founder points out that this natural practice has hardly been researched by the Government of India or anyone else. That is why Shubharambh took it to the scientists of ICAR-NISA.
html: In earlier times, homes were cleaned of germs with herbs and smoke rather than chemicals. Gums and resins such as guggul, dhuna and dhuwan (the resin of the Sal tree) were burned on cow-dung fire, and Bhimseni camphor was diffused through the rooms. The founder points out that this natural practice has hardly been researched by the Government of India or anyone else. That is why Shubharambh took it to the scientists of ICAR-NISA.

text: A 2007 peer-reviewed study (Nautiyal, Chauhan & Nene, Journal of Ethnopharmacology 114:446) found that one hour of medicinal smoke from havan samagri reduced airborne bacteria in a closed room by over 94%. The effect lasted up to 24 hours, and some pathogenic bacteria were still absent after 30 days.
html: A 2007 peer-reviewed study (Nautiyal, Chauhan & Nene, Journal of Ethnopharmacology 114:446) found that one hour of medicinal smoke from havan samagri reduced airborne bacteria in a closed room by over 94%. text: Ayurveda and folk practice describe camphor, guggul, loban, neem and tulsi as air-purifiers and insect-repellents, and the purpose of a havan as cleaning the environment. Some texts say camphor increases oxygen. We share these as traditional beliefs and do not claim them as proven facts.

text: Shubharambh approached the Government of India’s agricultural research system for proof that would let people trust an original product. The ICAR–National Institute of Secondary Agriculture (NISA) at Namkum, Ranchi, was the right home. It began in 1924 as the Indian Lac Research Institute, later became the Indian Institute of Natural Resins and Gums (IINRG), and in 2022 was renamed NISA with a wider mandate: helping farmers earn more from secondary agricultural produce and by-products.

text: Shubharambh means an auspicious beginning. We chose the name because we wanted to start again with things India once knew well.

text: From herbs and smoke to a question about purity
html: From herbs and smoke to a question about purity

text: Shubharambh started with a simple idea: why not work with the herbs and natural materials that nature gave us, and with the environment? In earlier times, homes were kept free of germs with jadi-buti and smoke: gums like guggul, dhuna, and dhuwan, the resin of the Sal tree. These are natural practices, but the Government of India and researchers worldwide have hardly studied them.
html: Shubharambh started with a simple idea: why not work with the herbs and natural materials that nature gave us, and with the environment? In earlier times, homes were kept free of germs with jadi-buti and smoke: gums like guggul, dhuna, and dhuwan, the resin of the Sal tree. These are natural practices, but the Government of India and researchers worldwide have hardly studied them.

text: That raised a harder question. Take Bhimseni camphor, which has many properties. How do we explore them? Where do we get certification, when synthetic material comes in from abroad and nobody can tell which is original? People compromise on quality without knowing it, because they have no way to judge it.

text: So we knocked on the government’s door and asked its scientists to tell us how the original can be identified, and which of its features actually work.

text: Honey purity is measured on about 17 to 18 parameters. One of them is pollen, which shows which flower the honey came from. If the dominant pollen belongs to one flower, the honey can be declared moringa honey, tulsi honey or karanj honey. Indian honey had rarely been certified this way before. FSSAI’s 2020 honey standard requires at least 45% pollen from the declared plant for a monofloral label, and Shubharambh aims for 60% or more.
html: Honey purity is measured on about 17 to 18 parameters. One of them is pollen, which shows which flower the honey came from. If the dominant pollen belongs to one flower, the honey can be declared moringa honey, tulsi honey or karanj honey. Indian honey had rarely been certified this way before. FSSAI’s 2020 honey standard requires at least 45% pollen from the declared plant for a monofloral label, and Shubharambh aims for 60% or more.

text: In 2020 a Centre for Science and Environment investigation found that 17 of 22 honey samples, including major brands, passed India’s routine tests but failed NMR. They contained sugar syrups designed to evade detection. FSSAI then added specific markers for rice syrup (SMR, TMR) and foreign oligosaccharides, and advanced labs use NMR profiling as an internationally accepted fingerprint.
html: In 2020 a Centre for Science and Environment investigation found that 17 of 22 honey samples, including major brands, passed India’s routine tests but failed NMR. They contained sugar syrups designed to evade detection. FSSAI then added specific markers for rice syrup (SMR, TMR) and foreign oligosaccharides, and advanced labs use NMR profiling as an internationally accepted fingerprint.
